reason: E1 supports faster Mn diffusion and formation of Mn-rich oxides, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for a critical 15 at.% Mn threshold, mechanical weakness of Mn oxides, or inability of Cr/Fe to compensate; E3 describes a more complex oxidation sequence where Mn is buried, which partially conflicts with the simple outward-diffusion picture.
premises: Mn diffuses faster than Cr, Fe, Co, Ni in CrFeCoNiMn
Rapid Mn outward diffusion leads to thick, porous Mn-rich oxide
Mn-rich oxide (Mn2O3/Mn3O4) is mechanically weak and prone to cracking/spallation
A critical Mn threshold (~15 at.%) exists for this instability
Cr and Fe cannot compensate for Mn-induced oxide instability
